text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
FRONT PAGE POLITICAL NEWS
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI
NOWA EUROPA

- France's President Jacques Chirac proposed to form a French-Polish strategic group to assist Poland's preparations to join NATO. The proposal was made during a meeting in Paris with Poland's President Aleksander Kwasniewski on Monday.
ECONOMIC AND MARKET STORIES
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- The World Bank would like Poland to maintain its economic growth rate at between four and five percent during the next five years. The bank is ready to grant Poland credits worth up to $400 million by 2000, World Bank's senior representative in Poland Paul Knotter said.

- More than 10 oil companies bought the second part of the privatisation memorandum of the Nafta Polska oil holding and their names will be disclosed at the holding's board meeting on Wednesday, Nafta Polska's spokesman Janusz Kwiatkowski said.

- Japan's NKK Corporation will open a branch office in Poland, NKK's deputy president Yamaga Motoo said. The concern is planning to buy steel products, cooperate with Poland's shipbuilding industry and subcontract Polish firms for international projects.

- The Huta Sendzimira steel mill in Krakow was turned into a joint stock company on May 1, 1997. The firm's privatisation plan provides for carving out three companies out of Sendzimir and separately sell minority stakes in them to strategic investors.
- Poland's national air carrier PLL LOT will cut ticket prices in the summer by up to 30 percent as part of its Flying Bus programme.

- Around 80 firms located in the Lublin province, eastern Poland, have already benefited from the Lublin credit Guaranttee fund (LFPK) co-funded by the Polish-British Industrial Development Programme. Hitherto LFPK underwrote credits totalling 4.8 million zlotys.

- Germany's Ultramarinfabrik Schindlerswerk paint maker has offered to buy a strategic stake in the Polifarb Kalisz (PK) paint maker in central Poland. PK's general shareholders meeting will vote on a share capital increase on May 22.
DZIENNIK PRAWA I GOSPODARKI

- The central bank president Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz will grant an operating licence to the Rzeszowski Bank Regionalny (RBR), the Rzeszow province regional bank. The bank has been formed as part of a programme to restructure the state-owned Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej (BGZ), the agricultural sector bank.
- Restructuring Poland's coke industry will cost 1.7 billion zlotys by 2005, deputy economy minister Jerzy Markowski said.

- Poland's Treasury Minister Miroslaw Pietrewicz has opposed the finance ministry's new tax on sales of shares held by the National Investment Funds (NFI). According to the treasury ministry's NFI department director Roman Galimski, Pietrewicz will intervene at the finance ministry in favour of preserving the funds' tax relief.
GAZETA WYBORCZA
- Foreign Trader Metalexport has bought a 53 percent stake in the Bison-Bial mechanical engineering firm in Bialystok worth 17.5 million zlotys.
ZYCIE
- Insurarer TUiR Polisa SA netted 3.7 million zlotys last year, 47 percent more than in 1995. Polisa's gross premium was 199.1 million zlotys, 61 percent more than in 1995.
-- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
